findings.label: M-01
findings.title: MEV / first-claimer front-run of winner-take-all nudge pot
findings.note: NEW at run phoenix-nft-staking-13. Distinct root cause from H-01 (mempool race vs. value-blind gate). Report generated and PoC (poc-MevFrontrunNudge.t.sol) validated passing; moved to submitted. [TRIAGE 2026-05-29] Accepted — valid finding. Mitigation: introduce a `minRewardPayout` parameter so the claimer can use AMM-style slippage mechanics to revert the transaction if their expected reward has been front-run/claimed. This protects an honest batch-minter from spending a large sum and receiving nothing. [TRIAGE 2026-05-30] ACCEPTED as residual (user triage 2026-05-30). Threat model verified against batchMint @ 9be4a87: (cond.2) claiming the nudge requires paying nudgeSize×mintPrice for real mints — the owner-pinned minter/dispatcher (story-009) make a free claim impossible (verified L257-259, L270); (cond.1) the minReward floor (L278-279) reverts the loser's batch atomically so a sniped user never overpays for a gone reward. Winner-take-all MEV capture remains by design and is accepted: nudge reward is a fraction of NFT mint cost, NFTs have no secondary market (only the staking pool), so a pure MEV bot cannot recoup in one tx — a front-runner who claims must genuinely join the protocol, reducing the issue to an ordinary gas auction among real participants. ACCEPTANCE INVARIANT (owner-operational, not code-enforced): keep the nudge pot < nudgeSize×mintPrice; if the yield funnel ever lets the pot exceed the cost of nudgeSize mints, pure-profit MEV returns. Also assumes a non-zero dispatcher mint price when the nudge is funded. [phoenix-nft-staking-16 RE-TRIAGE] The acceptance invariant 'keep pot < nudgeSize x mintPrice' does NOT bound loss if the minted NFTs carry realizable (resellable/redeemable) value: a searcher who realizes NFT value nets ~pot>0 for ANY pot size, so the giveaway is raced to zero on every refill — the 'NFTs have no secondary market' premise of the 2026-05-30 acceptance no longer holds if a market/redemption path exists (RETRIAGE-001 / ECON-002 / cross-ref F-01 lineage). Over-funding facet (PATTERN-002) is a non-obvious Law-3 owner footgun ('fund the incentive' silently == 'set a sweepable bounty'). Severity ceiling RE-CONFIRMED MEDIUM (NOT secretly High: no principal theft, honest minters still receive NFTs and story-015 minReward reverts a sniped honest caller atomically; loss bounded by owner funding; mempool ordering race, not an unconditional drain). [FIXED 2026-06-09] The core actionable harm was honest-user overpayment: a caller pays nudgeSize×mintPrice expecting a reward and receives nothing. This is fully closed by the `minReward` slippage floor (story-015): if the pot has been front-run, the batch reverts atomically and the honest user pays nothing. The remaining race — who wins the pot among qualifying batches — is an accepted gas-auction among genuine protocol participants, each of whom must pay the full mint cost. `nudgeSize` ensures no free-claim path exists (story-009). Marked fixed at HEAD 5f863d27 per owner triage 2026-06-09.

findings.humanReviewFlag: severity (Medium vs High) — confirmed-live with PoC; classifier resolved to MEDIUM (the dramatic 100x drain is Implausible-High only, gated on a post-exit inactivity window the attacker cannot control). High note preserved per conflicting-severity rule.
findings.note: NEW Medium at run phoenix-nft-staking-16 (cold --full re-scan of HEAD 5f863d2). emergencyWithdraw decrements totalStaked but skips _updatePool/_recomputeSchedule and never advances lastRewardTime, so the next _updatePool over-emits the reward budget to survivors by oldTotal/newTotal (100x). Solvency invariant holds throughout (over-draw clamped to rewardBudget at NFTStaker.sol:329) => value-leak / runway drain, NOT insolvency or principal theft. Violates the M-03 'no participation multiplier' Critical Invariant => cross-referenced as spec-conformance F-01 (carries the LIVE Medium per Law 1; NOT collapsed into QA noise). Submission-grade PoC validated PASS (2/2) by poc-validator against unmodified src @ 5f863d2 (workspace/phoenix-nft-staking/test/poc-M02-EmergencyWithdrawOverEmission.t.sol: test_M02_emergencyWithdraw_inflatesSurvivorEmission, test_M02_selfProfit_recoverPrincipalThenSidecarDrains; written GREEN). report-writer emitted the H/M submission; reportPath set. [TRIAGE 2026-06-09] Owner triage (2026-06-09): ACKNOWLEDGED / WON'T-FIX. NFTStaker is deployed and non-upgradeable; the only code fix (the pure-arithmetic rewardRate resize inside emergencyWithdraw) would require redeploying NFTStaker and migrating existing stakers to the new contract. NFTStaker exposes NO migrate-on-behalf mechanism — every position-moving entrypoint (stake/unstake/claim/emergencyWithdraw) is keyed to msg.sender; there is no depositFor / migrator role / batch — so a migration would force every staker to self-exit and re-stake. Owner accepts the residual over-emission rather than force a migration. Operational mitigation (recorded as the basis for won't-fix): the stale-rate window is closable on demand — the owner monitors EmergencyWithdrawn events and calls pullAndRefresh() (onlyOwner; triggers _recomputeSchedule, resizing rewardRate to current totalStaked) promptly after any emergency exit, bounding the leak to the owner's reaction gap; any stake/unstake/claim/topUp/setTargetAPY also resizes the rate. Finding remains VALID (value leak; solvency invariant holds) — status is won't-fix by owner decision, not an invalidation. Documentation note: the submission's 'collapses the runway / runway declines faster' wording (lines 19, 99) should be tightened — the harm is a value transfer to survivors / a failure to extend the runway per the variable-rate spec, NOT a faster-than-no-exit depletion (wall-clock time-to-depletion vs the no-exit baseline is unchanged). NOT a regression (wont-fix, never fixed — no fixed entry to reappear). wont-fix preserved (authoritative human triage). findings.label: M-01
findings.title: Linear-depletion rate-drift: per-interaction full-window re-spread leaves active stakers under-earning (~63.26% delivered) and the budget never depletes
findings.note: NEW Medium at run phoenix-nft-staking-18 (story-018, NFTStakerDepletion is a new linear-depletion contract). _recomputeSchedule/_syncBudget re-spread the full remaining budget over a fresh full depletion window on every interaction, so the depletion horizon never elapses and the budget is asymptotically re-deferred: active stakers receive only ~63.26% of the intended linear-depletion emission (~37% shortfall) and the budget never fully depletes. Same per-interaction full-window re-spread root-cause class as the phlimbo Linear-Depletion bug. Solvency-safe (payouts bounded by funded balance); value-delivery / protocol-function deviation, not theft. PoC PASSING (workspace/phoenix-nft-staking/test/PoC_DepletionRateDrift.t.sol, validated). Also tracked as spec-conformance F-18-01 (story-018 deviation) per Law 2 — carries the live Medium per Law 1. Submission emitted; status submitted. [TRIAGE 2026-06-25] ACKNOWLEDGED / WILL-FIX (owner triage 2026-06-25). Owner has accepted the finding and intends to fix it. AGREED DESIGN CLARIFICATION: a non-zero `pull` inflow means a new NFT was minted = a genuine budget increase, so RESTARTING the depletion window (windowEnd = now + windowSeconds) on a real inflow is INTENDED and is being KEPT. The fix only stops the window/rate recompute on interactions that did NOT change the budget. FIX PLAN recorded at reports/phoenix-nft-staking-18/fix-plan-M-01.md. Summary: (1) gate the `_syncBudget` recompute on inflow > 0 (move `_recomputeSchedule()` inside the `if (inflow > 0)` block; drop the unconditional and no-hook-branch recomputes); (2) remove the vestigial stake/unstake tail recomputes at L565/L585 (rate is totalStaked-independent — they only reset the deadline); (3) leave `_updatePool` per-interaction and the config-setter recomputes untouched. FIX IS SPECIFIC TO NFTStakerDepletion — must NOT be mirrored into NFTStaker / NFTStakerPriceScaled (those use the budget-independent APY/runway model where per-interaction recompute is correct). Finding remains VALID — status is acknowledged (will-fix) by owner decision, not an invalidation. Authoritative human triage: do NOT auto-overwrite on future runs. [FIXED 2026-06-25] Fixed upstream by commit 321d0a9 ([story-020] Fix NFTStakerDepletion rate-drift (audit M-01)), landed on top of the run-18 baseline 24acff8. The fix matches fix-plan-M-01.md EXACTLY, all three parts: (1) _syncBudget no-hook branch now just returns (no recompute) and the recompute is moved inside the `if (inflow > 0)` block; (2) stake tail _recomputeSchedule() removed; (3) unstake tail _recomputeSchedule() removed. _updatePool stays per-interaction; config-setter recomputes untouched; restart-on-mint (non-zero pull) preserved as intended. VERIFICATION (PoC-replay at 321d0a9): upstream shipped a regression test test/PoC_DepletionRateDrift.t.sol with 3 tests — test_M01_activeMatchesPassive_noRateDrift, test_M01_restartOnMint_preserved, test_M01_zeroInflowPullAndRefresh_isNoop — ALL PASS. findings.label: L-01
findings.title: InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator immutable stakedId lacks live-parity assertion vs staker.stakedId() — deploy-time mis-wire AND post-deploy setStakedId drift strands
findings.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-18 (story-019, new InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator). Constructor wires source/destination stakers without asserting stakedId/stakedToken consistency; an owner mis-wire can strand principal parked in the migrator mid-migration. Law-3 non-obvious deploy-time configuration footgun (in scope); no attacker, no theft, avoidable with a correct deploy. Bundled in QA report. Recommend a constructor cross-check asserting stakedToken/stakedId parity across the wired stakers. [phoenix-nft-staking-19 CONSOLIDATION — DEDUP-19-004 second strand, no new label/fingerprint] Root cause is one bug — the migrator's immutable stakedId carries no LIVE-parity assertion against the staker's owner-mutable stakedId(). Run-18 L-01 = the DEPLOY-TIME mis-wire strand. DEDUP-19-004 = the DYNAMIC POST-DEPLOY strand: a legitimate setStakedId reissue (onlyOwner + totalStaked==0-gated, i.e. only after users are parked) drifts staker.stakedId()->newId while migrator.stakedId stays oldId. CORRECTED IMPACT (supersedes the code-scanner's inverted narrative; per reports/phoenix-nft-staking-19/L-01-corrected-adjudication.md, severity-auditor source-traced): the physically-parked ERC1155 units are oldId and migrator.stakedId==oldId stays aligned with them forever, so claimTimedOut (transfers migrator.stakedId=oldId) STILL WORKS — the permissionless escape hatch is INTACT — and rescueERC1155's totalParked floor (balanceOf(this,migrator.stakedId)=balanceOf(oldId)) STILL guards the correct balance — the floor is INTACT. The ONLY real consequence is that migrateIn -> staker.depositFor pulls stakedToken.safeTransferFrom(migrator, staker, staker.stakedId()=newId) from a migrator holding only oldId -> REVERTS, so owner migrateIn re-injection BRICKS. Fully recoverable: parked users self-rescue via the permissionless claimTimedOut after migrationTimeout (1–30 days). No theft, no permanent loss, no floor void, no hatch kill -> stays LOW. CORRECTED REMEDIATION: assert migrator.stakedId == staker.stakedId() at the ENTRY of migrateIn (fail-loud before the re-injection loop), OR block setStakedId while totalParked>0 at the migrator. DO NOT repoint claimTimedOut/rescueERC1155 to read staker.stakedId() — that would BREAK the currently-working hatch/floor (migrator holds oldId, not newId). INCOMPLETE-FIX / RE-AUDIT TRAP (recorded, see WATCH-19-L01-incomplete-fix-trap): run-18 L-01's constructor-only cross-check does NOT close this dynamic strand (it passes at deploy then drifts on a later setStakedId); a constructor-only patch MUST NOT be auto-flipped to fixed — verify a live parity assert at migrateIn (or a totalParked>0 reissue guard) before flipping. Consolidation is NOT a drop (Law 1): recall preserved via this augmented note. lastSeenRun bumped to 19; still OPEN.

findings.label: L-02
findings.title: NFTStakerDepletion._syncBudget un-try/catch'd dispatcherHook.pull() lets an unauthorized hook DoS interactions and initiateMigration
findings.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-18 (story-018). _syncBudget calls dispatcherHook.pull() without try/catch; a reverting/unauthorized hook propagates the revert and bricks every _syncBudget caller — staker interactions and initiateMigration. Availability-only, owner-recoverable (re-point/clear the hook); no theft. Bundled in QA report. Recommend wrapping pull() in try/catch and skipping (with an event) on failure.

findings.label: L-03

findings.label: L-01
findings.title: NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor retains an unconditional tail window-restart; NatSpec 'parity with stake' stale post-story-020
findings.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-19 (story-020 residual). story-020 removed the permissionless stake/unstake tail _recomputeSchedule (closing M-01 rate-drift, fp b58b172e, fixed @321d0a9), but depositFor RETAINS an unconditional tail _recomputeSchedule (L767) that restarts windowEnd=now+windowSeconds on every call. CONFIRMED NOT A REGRESSION of M-01 (regressionRuledOut): depositFor is onlyMigrator (trusted, not permissionless), value-conserving, solvency-safe, and cannot be repeatably invoked by an attacker to grief the window — different function surface than M-01's stake/unstake tail. NatSpec 'parity with stake' is now stale/false (stake no longer recomputes). Recommend gating the depositFor tail recompute on inflow>0 and correcting the NatSpec. Carries faithfulness:true, routed to spec-conformance as F-19-01 (Law 2, honest Low). Cross-ref M-01 (b58b172e).

findings.label: L-02
findings.title: NFTStakerDepletion.finalizeAndReset revives pool to Active without re-arming the depletion window; organic stake earns zero until owner re-arm
findings.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-19 (story-020 consequence surfaced as footgun). finalizeAndReset revives a drained Migrating pool to Active (L778-784) but does NOT recompute the schedule; post-story-020 stake() no longer auto-rearms, so a revive-then-organic-stake sequence (no depositFor re-seed via the self-healing migrator path) emits ZERO rewards until owner re-arms via setDepletionWindow/topUp. Value never lost; emissions pause until re-arm; principal untouched. Non-obvious asymmetric Law-3 owner footgun (migrator path self-heals, organic path does not). Recommend finalizeAndReset re-arm the window or emit a NEEDS-REARM signal. Carries faithfulness:true, routed to spec-conformance as F-19-03 (Law 2).

findings.label: L-03
findings.title: unstake performs outbound ERC1155 transfer before tail _recomputeSchedule; read-only reentrancy view-inconsistency window (no in-scope consumer)
findings.note: NEW Low/implausible-High at run phoenix-nft-staking-19. In unstake (NFTStaker AND the NFTStakerPriceScaled copy) the outbound ERC1155 safeTransferFrom (onERC1155Received on a caller-chosen recipient) executes BEFORE the tail _recomputeSchedule, so during the callback totalStaked is decremented while rewardRate/windowEnd still reflect the OLD pool — value-reporting views (currentRewardRate/runwaySeconds/totalNFTValue) return a transiently inconsistent snapshot. State-changing reentry is blocked by contract-wide nonReentrant; impact requires an external oracle-style consumer of these views mid-callback (NONE known in scope). Kept-not-dropped per Law 1 (victim is a hypothetical downstream integrator). Recommend moving the outbound transfer AFTER _recomputeSchedule (CEI). Re-escalate only if an in-scope oracle/integrator of these views appears.

findings.label: L-04
findings.title: DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol hardcodes assumed DISPATCHER_INDEX / USDC nudge token with no on-chain deploy-time cross-check against dispatcher.primeToken()
findings.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-19. DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol hardcodes DISPATCHER_INDEX (ASSUMED=4, L48) and USDC as the nudge token; broadcast guards do NOT verify on-chain that nudgeToken != the pinned dispatcher's primeToken() (only enforced at batchMint RUNTIME). A wrong index pins the batcher to the wrong dispatcher/payment asset; failure surfaces only at batchMint runtime (equality guard reverts) -> redeploy/repoint. No funds lost; operational rework only. Non-obvious deploy-config Law-3 footgun, mitigated by NatSpec confirm + runtime revert. Recommend an on-chain deploy-time assert that nudgeToken != dispatcher.primeToken() and that the resolved dispatcher at DISPATCHER_INDEX is intended, failing the broadcast rather than deferring to runtime.

findings.label: Q-01
findings.title: NFTStakerMigrator stores a dead immutable stakedId never referenced by migrate(); implies a parity guarantee the code does not enforce
findings.note: NEW QA at run phoenix-nft-staking-19. NFTStakerMigrator stores an immutable stakedId (L44/L62) that migrate() never references and never asserts equal across old/new stakers; a mismatch is a hard revert with clean atomic rollback (no fund loss). Dead immutable misleadingly implies a parity guarantee. DISTINCT contract and DISTINCT failure mode from the InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator strand (clean DoS-revert here vs migrateIn-brick there) — kept SEPARATE from L-01 (e7bccb02), NOT consolidated. Recommend either wiring the immutable into a real cross-staker parity assert in migrate() or removing it.
